paper.title: Long-term consequences of workplace bullying on sickness absence
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement is printed. The acknowledgement note says: …

registers.name_in_paper: The Danish Register for Evaluation of Marginalization (DREAM)
registers.role: outcomes (weeks of sickness absence, employment, out of the labor force) and controls (pre-2006 sickness absence and unemployment history)
variables_mentioned: weekly information on everyone in Denmark who collects government benefits

registers.years: pre-2006 for controls; 2011 for the outcome
registers.role: controls (pre-2006 mental or behavioral diagnosis) and outcome (mental or behavioral diagnosis in 2011)
variables_mentioned: mental or behavioral disorder diagnoses (ICD-10 code F)

registers.name_in_paper: Danish registry data on prescription drug use
registers.role: controls (pre-2006 antidepressant and psycholeptic use) and outcomes (purchases 2007-2011)

registers.name_in_paper: The Integrated Database for Labor Market Research (IDA)
registers.role: sample frame for the Appendix A attrition analysis: all individuals registered as working at the respondents' workplaces

registers.name_in_paper: the Danish registry data (demographics, socio-economic status, current employment, workplace identifiers, somatic and psychiatric diagnoses from general hospitals)

registers.role: treatment (NAQ-R bullying indicator) and survey outcomes (self-rated health, presenteeism), plus personality (PANAS, SOC) and COPSOQ II work environment scales
variables_mentioned: Setterlind and Larsson's (1995) Sense of Coherence (SOC) scale

linkages: The survey data are merged with the Danish registry data using the respondents' civil registration number.
Respondents are matched to workplaces (physical places, not companies) via workplace identifiers in the registries; the 54 companies map to 104 workplaces used for the workplace fixed effects.
Appendix A compares respondents with all individuals registered as working at the same workplaces in IDA; the non-respondents' civil registration numbers are not available.

sample.universe: Employees of Danish companies that volunteered for the 2006 Bullying Cohort Study run by the National Research Centre for the Working Environment
selection_rules: 90 companies (28 private, 62 public) answered an open online invitation on the websites of professional organizations
only companies with more than 30 employees were asked to attend, leaving 79 eligible companies, of which 60 agreed to participate (a few daycare centers with fewer than 30 employees were allowed in)
3358 people responded to the questionnaire, a response rate of 45.9%
restrict to the 54 companies that had more than ten employees respond, which map to 136 workplaces in the registries
delete workplaces where fewer than three employees respond to the bullying items, leaving 54 companies in 104 workplaces with 3227 respondents
delete 27 respondents who the data indicate are retired before the survey period
delete 18 respondents who did not respond to the NAQ-R
final sample: 3182 employees in 104 workplaces (2169 women, 1013 men)
public sector subsample used in Table 10 and Fig. 3, where DREAM records absence from day one
the log wage income analysis is restricted to individuals in employment
sample.n_individuals: 3182 (2169 women, 1013 men); 228 classified as bullied and 2954 as non-bullied

construction_notes: Bullying: a respondent is a target if they report at least two negative acts daily or weekly during the past six months on the 21-item NAQ-R; 7% of respondents qualify; the NAQ-R is asked before the word bullying appears in the questionnaire.

Long-term sickness absence: weeks of sickness absence accumulated annually in excess of three weeks, counting only spells of at least three weeks, 2001-2011; DREAM registers only the benefits covered by the local authority, so shorter spells are unobserved for private sector employees.
For public sector employees absence is observed from day one, which is used in Table 10 and Fig. 3.
Employment: at least six months of accumulated work experience within the given year (a nine-month alternative is reported in footnotes).
Out of the labor force: more than six months outside DREAM with no public transfer observed and fewer than 25 accumulated weeks of work experience.
Antidepressants: ATC code N06A; psycholeptics: ATC code N05; purchases measured 2001-2005 for controls and 2007-2011 for outcomes.
Mental or behavioral disorder: ICD-10 chapter F diagnosis, measured pre-2006 as a control and in 2011 as an outcome.
Self-rated health: 'How good do you find your health?' on a five-point Likert scale recoded one to five, five indicating excellent health.
All conditioning variables are measured in 2005 or earlier to minimize bias due to endogeneity.
Workplace: defined as a physical place rather than a company, because a company can have multiple branches.

Personality: PANAS positive and negative affectivity (one item, 'Alert', excluded) and a nine-item Sense of Coherence scale; all three factors extracted by confirmatory principal component analysis with scores obtained by the regression method.
Work environment: COPSOQ II scales extracted by confirmatory factor analysis and grouped as in Pejtersen et al. (2010); Cronbach's alphas range between 0.535 and 0.878.
Standard errors are clustered at the workplace level throughout.

links.pointer_quote: Our results show that, while gender does not explain exposure to bullying once we condition on workplace fixed effects, a significant and negative relationship only exists between workplace bullying and sickness absence for women.

claims.statement: Conditional on individual, work-related and previous-health characteristics and workplace fixed effects, being male does not significantly change the probability of being a target of workplace bullying.

definition.value: Registry indicator for being male, measured in 2005.

timing.value: Measured in 2005, the year before the bullying survey.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the respondent reports at least two negative acts daily or weekly during the past six months on the 21-item NAQ-R in the 2006 questionnaire.

timing.value: Measured in the 2006 survey (September-November 2006).

units.value: change in the probability of being a target of bullying (marginal effect) per unit of the regressor

estimand.target_population: Employees of the 104 sampled Danish workplaces
estimand.time_horizon: conditioning characteristics measured in 2005; bullying measured in the 2006 survey

population.description: The 3182 respondents to the 2006 Bullying Cohort Study at 54 Danish companies mapped to 104 workplaces.
population.period: bullying measured in 2006; all conditioning variables measured in 2005 or earlier
subgroups_defined: Never Bullied / Newly Bullied / Always Bullied / Previously Bullied
population.selection: Employees of 90 self-selecting Danish companies that answered an open online invitation; restricted to the 54 companies with more than ten respondents, then to workplaces with at least three respondents to the bullying items, excluding respondents retired before the survey period and those who did not answer the NAQ-R; implicitly conditioned on being employed in the survey weeks of 2006. Response rate 45.9%.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in self-reported exposure to at least two negative acts weekly or daily on the NAQ-R in 2006 between employees of the same workplace, conditional on pre-2006 individual, work-related and health characteristics. No exogenous shock, instrument or policy change is used.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional independence (selection on observables): once individual characteristics X, work-related characteristics W, previous health H and a workplace fixed effect are conditioned on, exposure to bullying is unrelated to the remaining determinants of the outcome.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper motivates the conditioning set explicitly, shows in Table 4 that few observables predict bullying once workplace fixed effects are included, and shows in Tables 5-8 that the coefficient is almost unchanged as the conditioning set is expanded.

key_assumptions.assumption: No reverse causality from sickness absence to being recorded as a target of bullying; for the propensity model this is embodied in measuring every conditioning variable in 2005 or earlier.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Fig. 1 shows no spike in weekly sickness absence before the survey week; Table 1 shows no significant difference in long-term sickness absence between targets and non-targets from 2001 to 2005; Fig. 3 repeats the exercise for public employees including short spells.

key_assumptions.assumption: Persistence of earlier bullying episodes does not drive the estimates: targets are no more likely than non-targets to have been bullied before 2006.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Mean comparison of previously-bullied status between targets and non-targets; Fig. 2 and Appendix Table D split respondents into Never, Newly, Always and Previously Bullied.

key_assumptions.assumption: A latent confounder remains: pre-exposure personality traits are unobserved and the authors concede they cannot reject that bullying is a consequence of personal characteristics.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Probed only partially: Table 7 adds contemporaneously measured personality scales (PANAS affectivity, Sense of Coherence) and Table 8 adds COPSOQ II work environment scales, but the paper states these are themselves likely affected by exposure to bullying.

key_assumptions.assumption: Sample selection: the estimation sample is conditioned on working at a participating workplace, responding to the questionnaire and being employed in the survey weeks of 2006.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Discussed in Section 4.1 and Appendix A, which runs a probit of response propensity on registry characteristics; the authors argue the implied bias is downwards.

key_assumptions.assumption: Measurement error in the NAQ-R bullying indicator (under-reporting of negative acts; subjective evaluation of the items) biases the estimates towards zero rather than away from it.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Argument only: the paper notes under-reporting and non-response patterns and states the resulting bias is downwards; no correction or bounding exercise is reported.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the respondent reports on the 21-item Negative Acts Questionnaire-Revised (NAQ-R) that they have been subject to at least two negative acts daily or weekly within the past six months. Taken from the 2006 Bullying Cohort Study questionnaire (fielded September-November 2006); 7% of respondents are classified as exposed.

timing.value: Measured in the 2006 survey, referring to the six months preceding the questionnaire (latter half of 2006).

outcome.label: Weeks of sickness absence 2011 (short- and long-term, public sector)

register_source.value: DREAM (Danish Register for Evaluation of Marginalization): weekly benefit records

definition.value: Weeks of sickness absence accumulated in the calendar year measured from week one, containing both short-term and long-term spells. Available only for public sector employees, for whom DREAM records absence from day one.

timing.value: Calendar year 2011, i.e. 5 year(s) after exposure to bullying is measured in the 2006 survey.

units.value: weeks of sickness absence per year, counted from week one

estimand.target_population: Male public sector employees among the respondents of the 104 sampled Danish workplaces
estimand.time_horizon: sickness absence in 2011, 5 year(s) after bullying is observed in 2006

population.description: Male public sector employees among the 2006 Bullying Cohort Study respondents (522 observations).
population.period: bullying measured 2006; outcome measured in calendar year 2011
subgroups_defined: Never Bullied / Newly Bullied / Always Bullied / Previously Bullied
population.selection: Employees of 90 self-selecting Danish companies that answered an open online invitation; restricted to the 54 companies with more than ten respondents, then to workplaces with at least three respondents to the bullying items, excluding respondents retired before the survey period and those who did not answer the NAQ-R; implicitly conditioned on being employed in the survey weeks of 2006. Response rate 45.9%. Further restricted to public sector employees, for whom DREAM records absence from day one.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional variation in self-reported exposure to at least two negative acts weekly or daily on the NAQ-R in 2006 between employees of the same workplace, conditional on pre-2006 individual, work-related and health characteristics. No exogenous shock, instrument or policy change is used.

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional independence (selection on observables): once individual characteristics X, work-related characteristics W, previous health H and a workplace fixed effect are conditioned on, exposure to bullying is unrelated to the remaining determinants of the outcome.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper motivates the conditioning set explicitly, shows in Table 4 that few observables predict bullying once workplace fixed effects are included, and shows in Tables 5-8 that the coefficient is almost unchanged as the conditioning set is expanded.

key_assumptions.assumption: No reverse causality: sickness absence before the 2006 survey does not cause being recorded as a target of bullying.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Fig. 1 shows no spike in weekly sickness absence before the survey week; Table 1 shows no significant difference in long-term sickness absence between targets and non-targets from 2001 to 2005; Fig. 3 repeats the exercise for public employees including short spells.

key_assumptions.assumption: Persistence of earlier bullying episodes does not drive the estimates: targets are no more likely than non-targets to have been bullied before 2006.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Mean comparison of previously-bullied status between targets and non-targets; Fig. 2 and Appendix Table D split respondents into Never, Newly, Always and Previously Bullied.

key_assumptions.assumption: A latent confounder remains: pre-exposure personality traits are unobserved and the authors concede they cannot reject that bullying is a consequence of personal characteristics.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Probed only partially: Table 7 adds contemporaneously measured personality scales (PANAS affectivity, Sense of Coherence) and Table 8 adds COPSOQ II work environment scales, but the paper states these are themselves likely affected by exposure to bullying.

implies_edges.to: Weeks of sickness absence 2011 (short- and long-term, public sector)

key_assumptions.assumption: Sample selection: the estimation sample is conditioned on working at a participating workplace, responding to the questionnaire and being employed in the survey weeks of 2006.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Discussed in Section 4.1 and Appendix A, which runs a probit of response propensity on registry characteristics; the authors argue the implied bias is downwards.

key_assumptions.assumption: Measurement error in the NAQ-R bullying indicator (under-reporting of negative acts; subjective evaluation of the items) biases the estimates towards zero rather than away from it.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Argument only: the paper notes under-reporting and non-response patterns and states the resulting bias is downwards; no correction or bounding exercise is reported.

heterogeneity.finding: In the public sector subsample, where absence is observed from week one, the estimates are slightly larger than in the full sample, which the paper attributes to public sector employees having more long-term sickness absence.

Splitting the sample by gender (Table 6), a positive and significant relationship between bullying and long-term sickness absence appears only for women, in 2007-2009; for men every coefficient is small and insignificant. The paper notes it cannot reject a Chow test of equal coefficients for men and women.

claims.statement: Among men, being a target of workplace bullying in 2006 is not significantly associated with being out of the labor force in 2011.

definition.value: Indicator equal to one if the respondent reports on the 21-item Negative Acts Questionnaire-Revised (NAQ-R) that they have been subject to at least two negative acts daily or weekly within the past six months. Taken from the 2006 Bullying Cohort Study questionnaire (fielded September-November 2006); 7% of respondents are classified as exposed.

timing.value: Measured in the 2006 survey, referring to the six months preceding the questionnaire (latter half of 2006).

register_source.value: DREAM (Danish Register for Evaluation of Marginalization)

definition.value: Dummy equal to one if the individual has spent more than six months outside DREAM, in which case no public transfer is observed, and more than 25 weeks of work experience are not accumulated either (employment = 0).

timing.value: Measured in 2011, 5 year(s) after bullying is observed in 2006.

units.value: probability of being out of the labor force in the given year
